To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EASSRs to AM and PWM high-rate pulse-trains account for temporal effects at 9 kpps and result in electrophysiological threshold values that correlate well with behavioral thresholds at 9 kpp.

(1) EASSR thresholds derived from amplitude-modulated ( AM) and pulse-width- modulated ( PWM) high-rate pulse train stimulation correlate well with behavioral thresholds for the same stimuli; (2) the new two-sample Hotelling test is a reliable and robust statistical method for response analysis; and (3) the two-sample Hotelling method can be used to reliably determine EASSR thresholds even in the presence of large stimulus artifacts.

electrophysiological threshold measurements based on EASSRs to AM and PWM pulse trains at a carrier rate of 900 pps correlate very well with the behavioral T level at 900 pps, and that a new statistical method that does not require stimulus artifact removal can be used to reliably determine electrophysiological response thresholds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of improved methods for the measurement of electrophysiological T levels in cochlear-implant users.
the development of improved electrophysiology-based methods for the estimation of T levels at high pulse rates, which are of great interest in cochlear implants.

the development of an improved electrophysiology-based method to determine reliable and accurate electrophysiological and behavioral thresholds at high pulse rates for the optimization of cochlear implant stimulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed new statistical method for EASSR detection is very useful for the determination of electrophysiological stimulation thresholds.

the new statistical method for the determination of electrophysiological T levels based on a two sample Hotelling T2-test is robust in the presences of stimulus artifacts and that the new stimuli result in electrophysiological measures that correlate well with behavioral thresholds.

EASSR thresholds are a valid and reliable measure of the electrically evoked neural activity in the cochlear nucleus and that the new statistical method is a valid and reliable method for determining electrophysiological T levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EASSRs are an excellent tool for the determination of electrophysiological T levels and that the proposed statistical method is a very promising tool for the analysis of these EASSRs.
EASSRs can be measured at 900 ppsm and that the proposed statistical method is a promising tool to measure electrophysiological T levels in humans.

we were able to improve the correlation of electrophysiological and behavioral thresholds at 900 ppm by using modulated high-rate stimuli and by using a new statistical method that does not require stimulus artifact removal.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of AM and PWM high-rate pulse train stimuli with a new statistical method of response detection results in a very good correlation between electrophysical thresholds and behavioral thresholds at 900 ps.

electrophysiological threshold measurements based on EASSRs can be used for the assessment of the electrical stimulation levels in the cochlea and that this can be done with high reliability and without the need for stimulus artifact removal.

EASSR measurements to AM and PWM high-rate pulse train stimuli provide a reliable electrophysiology-based measure for T level estimation at high pulse rates, which is not possible using conventional EASSRs to low-rate pulse trains.
